summary: This note is a long Wikipedia-derived overview of the British Empire, covering its origins in the 16th and 17th centuries, its expansion through colonies in the Americas, India, Australia and New Zealand, and the slave trade that underpinned its Caribbean colonies. It also traces the empire's 19th-century peak under Pax Britannica, its territorial maximum after World War I, and its decolonisation after World War II, ending with the Commonwealth of Nations and the remaining overseas territories. Much of the text is repeated across the note.
one_line: Overview of the British Empire's origins, expansion, slave trade, decolonisation and the modern Commonwealth and overseas territories.
key_facts: Britain formed an alliance with Japan in 1902 and with France and Russia in 1904 and 1907, respectively, amid fears about defending the empire while keeping 'splendid isolation'.
Britain was responsible for transporting 3.5 million African slaves to the Americas until the abolition of the slave trade in 1807, a third of all slaves transported across the Atlantic.
The Slavery Abolition Act passed in 1833 abolished slavery in the British Empire on 1 August 1834.
The Battle of Plassey in 1757, led by Robert Clive, left the British East India Company in control of Bengal and as the major military and political power in India.
Britain announced in 1947 that it would withdraw from the British Mandate of Palestine in 1948 and leave the matter to the United Nations.
Under the Treaty of Versailles signed in 1919, the empire reached its greatest extent, adding 1,800,000 square miles and 13 million new subjects.
By 1922 the British Empire held sway over about 458 million people, one-fifth of the world's population at the time.
Lord Mountbatten, the last Viceroy, brought forward the date of Indian independence to 15 August 1947.
Burma and Sri Lanka gained independence in 1948; India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka joined the Commonwealth, while Burma chose not to join.
The transfer of Hong Kong to China in 1997 marked for many the end of the British Empire.
Britain retains sovereignty over 14 overseas territories; Bermuda (1995), Gibraltar (2002) and the Falkland Islands (2013) voted to remain under British sovereignty.
The Treaty of Waitangi was signed on 6 February 1840 by Captain William Hobson and around 40 Maori chiefs.
In 1875, Benjamin Disraeli's Conservative government bought Isma'il Pasha's 44 percent shareholding in the Suez Canal for £4 million.
The Act of Union in 1840 created the Province of Canada, and the British North America Act, 1867 formed the Dominion of Canada.
Melbourne became for a time the richest city in the world during the Victorian gold rushes, and the largest city after London in the British Empire.

entities.name: Royal African Company
entities.role: Company inaugurated two years before the Royal African Company's monopoly on supplying slaves to British Caribbean colonies, granted by King Charles

entities.name: East India Company
entities.role: English company that competed for trade and gradually increased its territories in India; its end was precipitated by the Indian Rebellion

entities.name: French East India Company
entities.role: French counterpart of the English East India Company during the Carnatic Wars

entities.name: Robert Clive
entities.role: British leader who defeated the Nawab of Bengal and his French allies at the Battle of Plassey in 1757

entities.name: Clement Attlee
entities.role: Labour prime minister elected in 1945 who moved quickly to tackle Indian independence

entities.name: Lord Mountbatten
entities.role: Newly appointed and last Viceroy who brought forward the date of Indian independence to 15 August 1947

entities.name: John Cabot
entities.role: Explorer commissioned by Henry VII in 1496 who sailed in 1497 and made landfall on Newfoundland

entities.name: Humphrey Gilbert
entities.role: Explorer granted a patent by Elizabeth I in 1578 who claimed Newfoundland for England in 1583

entities.name: Walter Raleigh
entities.role: Half-brother of Humphrey Gilbert who founded the Roanoke colony in 1584

entities.name: Abel Tasman
entities.role: Dutch explorer who first discovered New Zealand in 1642

entities.name: James Cook
entities.role: Explorer who visited New Zealand, claimed the eastern coast of Australia in 1770 and named it New South Wales

entities.name: Joseph Banks
entities.role: Cook's botanist who recommended Botany Bay as the site for a penal settlement in 1778

entities.name: Benjamin Disraeli
entities.role: Conservative leader whose government bought the Suez Canal shareholding in 1875

entities.name: Isma'il Pasha
entities.role: Indebted Egyptian ruler who sold his 44 percent shareholding in the Suez Canal

entities.name: William Hobson
entities.role: Captain who signed the Treaty of Waitangi on 6 February 1840

entities.name: John Smith
entities.role: Captain who led England's first permanent settlement in the Americas at Jamestown in 1607

entities.name: Willem Janszoon
entities.role: Dutch explorer who discovered the western coast of Australia for Europeans in 1606

entities.name: Queen Elizabeth II
entities.role: Monarch shared by the sixteen Commonwealth realms as head of state

entities.name: Napoleon III
entities.role: Ruler under whom the Suez Canal opened in 1869

entities.name: Virginia Company
entities.role: Company that managed the Jamestown settlement; its charter was revoked in 1624

entities.name: Commonwealth of Nations
entities.role: Non-political, voluntary association of equal members, most former British colonies and protectorates, with about 2.2 billion people

entities.name: Indian National Congress
entities.role: Political party campaigning for independence that favoured a unified secular Indian state

entities.name: Muslim League
entities.role: Political party that desired a separate Islamic state for Muslim-majority regions

entities.name: New Zealand Company
entities.role: Company that in 1839 announced plans to buy land and establish colonies in New Zealand

entities.name: Suez Canal
entities.role: Waterway opened in 1869 that became the 'jugular vein of the Empire'

entities.name: Palestine
entities.role: Former British Mandate where Arab and Jewish communities lived, and which the UN partitioned into Jewish and Arab states

entities.name: Jamaica
entities.role: Island annexed by England from the Spanish in 1655

entities.name: Treaty of Waitangi
entities.role: Treaty signed in 1840 considered New Zealand's founding document, though interpretations of its versions remain disputed

entities.name: Pax Britannica
entities.role: Period of relative peace in Europe and the world (1815-1914) during which the British Empire became the global hegemon

entities.name: Slavery Abolition Act
entities.role: 1833 Act that abolished slavery in the British Empire on 1 August 1834

entities.name: Slave Trade Act
entities.role: 1807 Act by Parliament that abolished the slave trade in the empire

entities.name: Treaty of Versailles
entities.role: 1919 treaty under which the empire reached its greatest extent
